title: Beestat — Ecobee Detail
description: Live thermostat and per-room ecobee data archived from beestat.io. Runtime is stored as seconds per 5-minute interval; hours = sum/3600.

list.name: sensor
list.label: Rooms
list.query:
import "influxdata/influxdb/schema"
schema.tagValues(bucket: "beestat", tag: "sensor_name",
  predicate: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor", start: -30d)

panels.title: Indoor
panels.description: The thermostat's own reading, most recent 5-minute sample.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "indoor_temperature")
  |> group() |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])

from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "indoor_humidity")
  |> group() |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])

panels.title: Outdoor
panels.description: Outdoor temperature from ecobee's weather service, not a local sensor.

from(bucket: "beestat")

from(bucket: "beestat")

panels.title: Comfort Profile
panels.description: Which ecobee comfort profile is in effect (Home / Sleep / WFH / away).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "climate")
  |> group() |> last()

panels.title: Room Spread
panels.description: Warmest minus coolest of the SELECTED rooms, right now. This is the number the fan-circulation experiment is trying to shrink. Note the whole-house figure is dominated by the Server closet and the basement Puzzle Room — use the Rooms variable to compare a meaningful pair.

targets.query:
base = from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"]) |> last() |> group()
base
  |> reduce(identity: {mx: -200.0, mn: 200.0, _value: 0.0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        mx: if r._value > accumulator.mx then r._value else accumulator.mx,
        mn: if r._value < accumulator.mn then r._value else accumulator.mn,
        _value: (if r._value > accumulator.mx then r._value else accumulator.mx)
              - (if r._value < accumulator.mn then r._value else accumulator.mn)}))

panels.title: Sensors Reporting
panels.description: Distinct sensors that reported in this range. Expect 11; a lower number means a sensor dropped off or its battery died.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"]) |> last() |> group() |> count()

panels.title: Room Temperatures — now
panels.description: Current temperature per room.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"]) |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "sensor_name"])

panels.title: Room Temperatures — mean over range
panels.description: Average per room across the whole range. The ranking is the balance story: which rooms sit persistently hot or cold, independent of any single moment. Over 7 days this spans roughly 16 degF.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"]) |> mean()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "sensor_name"])

panels.title: Cool
panels.description: Compressor hours in cooling mode over the range.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "compressor_1" or r._field == "compressor_mode"
        or r._field == "auxiliary_heat_1" or r._field == "fan")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.compressor_mode == "cool")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_value: r.compressor_1 / 3600.0}))
  |> sum()

panels.description: Compressor hours in heating mode (heat pump).

from(bucket: "beestat")

  |> sum()

panels.title: Aux (propane)
panels.description: Auxiliary heat hours. This system's aux is the PROPANE furnace, not electric resistance, so this is a direct proxy for propane burned.

targets.query:

panels.title: Fan
panels.description: Total blower hours, including circulation with no heat or cool call.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")

panels.title: Equipment
panels.description: What the system actually did, per 5-minute interval.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "compressor_1" or r._field == "compressor_mode"
        or r._field == "auxiliary_heat_1" or r._field == "fan")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, Equipment:
        if r.auxiliary_heat_1 > 0.0 then "Aux (propane)"
        else if r.compressor_1 > 0.0 and r.compressor_mode == "cool" then "Cool"
        else if r.compressor_1 > 0.0 and r.compressor_mode == "heat" then "Heat"
        else if r.fan > 0.0 then "Fan only"
        else "Off" }))

panels.title: Temperatures & Setpoints
panels.description: Indoor against outdoor with the active setpoints. Setpoints are drawn as steps because they change discretely with the schedule.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "indoor_temperature")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "Indoor")

from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "outdoor_temperature")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "Outdoor")

from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "setpoint_cool")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "Cool setpoint")

from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "setpoint_heat")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "Heat setpoint")

panels.title: Room Temperatures
panels.description: Every selected room over time. The equivalent of beestat's Sensor Detail.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"])

panels.title: Occupancy
panels.description: Motion-detected occupancy per room. Useful for checking whether the rooms that run hot are the ones actually being used.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "occupancy")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: if r._value then "Occupied" else "Empty",
        sensor_name: r.sensor_name}))
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"])

panels.title: Room Spread over time
panels.description: Warmest minus coolest of the selected rooms, over time. Falling spread means better circulation. This is the primary A/B metric for fan settings.

targets.query:
base = from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group(columns: ["_time"])
hi = base |> max() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"]) |> rename(columns: {_value: "hi"})
lo = base |> min() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"]) |> rename(columns: {_value: "lo"})
join(tables: {h: hi, l: lo}, on: ["_time"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r.hi - r.lo}))
  |> group()

panels.title: Deviation from Thermostat (mean)
panels.description: How far each room sits above or below the thermostat's own reading, averaged over the range. The thermostat only controls to ITS location, so these offsets are what every other room actually experiences. Large positive values are rooms that stay hot when cooling satisfies.

targets.query:
therm = from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature" and r.sensor_name == "Kitchen Ecobee")
  |> group() |> mean() |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_sensor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "temperature")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_name =~ /^$${sensor:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["sensor_name"]) |> mean()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: r._value - therm._value}))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "sensor_name"])

panels.title: Fan hours per day
panels.description: Total blower hours per day, and how many of those had NO heating or cooling call — that portion is pure circulation cost. A flat 24 means the fan was set to ON rather than AUTO. Use this to compare fan_min_on_time settings against the Room Spread panel above.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_fan")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r._value / 3600.0}))
  |> group() |> set(key: "_field", value: "Fan")

from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_fan" or r._field == "sum_compressor_cool_1"
        or r._field == "sum_compressor_heat_1" or r._field == "sum_auxiliary_heat_1")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: (r.sum_fan - r.sum_compressor_cool_1
        - r.sum_compressor_heat_1 - r.sum_auxiliary_heat_1) / 3600.0}))
  |> group() |> set(key: "_field", value: "Fan with no call")

panels.title: Fan minimum on time (Home Assistant)
panels.description: The ecobee fan_min_on_time setting, read from Home Assistant — beestat does not expose it. Note this only applies in AUTO mode; while the fan mode is ON the setting is inert, which is why runtime can sit at 24h/day with this reading 10.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "homeassistant")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.friendly_name == "Kitchen Ecobee Fan minimum on time")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value")
  |> group() |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "min/hr")
